It follows each HK1 by 5 s

Two-processor passivation arm: the EPS controller's key and the OBC's EOL_ARM, the latch confirmed before PASSIVATE_EXECUTE is accepted. On PASSIVATE_ARM the software shall read EOL_STATE (0x7C) and proceed only with bit 0 (ARMED) clear and bit 2 (fuse intact) set; write the key to EOL_KEY (0x7E): 0x3C then 0xC3 within 1 s (the controller holds bit 3, KEY, for 10 s); raise EOL_ARM (PF4) within those 10 s; confirm bit 0 set within 2 s, then drop EOL_ARM. A refused key, a latch not set or an unanswered controller is reported (PASSIVATE_ARM fails, nothing else driven). PASSIVATE_EXECUTE is accepted only with the latch confirmed and the arm live (600 s) (RID P3E-11; SQSO-ICD-001 1.5 §4.6)

GNSS state frame after each session with a fix and on GET_HOUSEKEEPING (after HK2): `GNS N=<session> WK=<GPS week> TOW=<ms> X= Y= Z=<m> VX= VY= VZ=<mm/s> VDT=<s> Q=<GGA quality> SV=<satellites> PD=<PDOP x 10> AGE=<s>` (SQSO-TLM-001 §4.4.2). The ECEF velocity is derived from the session's first accepted fix and the latest (a chord of 10 to 120 s) with the Earth-fixed acceleration (point mass, J2, Coriolis, centrifugal) by Simpson's rule: method error below 0.01 m/s; `-` without a chord. Through the downlink's inhibits and duty limit; the latest fix is kept for the repeat (RID LV-04)

DEPLOY_SENSE (PE2) read as the hardware drives it: high = DS2 released, low = stowed, no internal pull (the EPS's 1 MΩ source; SQSO-ICX-001 D §3.7). Released for 10 s without a break latches separation until the next reset; after the latch a stowed reading (an open line) restarts neither the RF silence nor the deployment wait and is counted (HK2 `SEP`). Before the latch a stowed reading holds both timers at zero (the bench). Separation established before a reset (the separation flag in a non-ARMED deployment record, or the served RF silence in its record) latches the reading at boot, so after a reset a stowed reading restarts neither timer either (a power-losing reset still restarts the 30-minute wait from zero); GSE ARM clears it (RID SMA-B02 reopened, BOARD_FMEA BF-OBC-18). SOLAR_SENSE: low = both wings deployed, no internal pull. No internal pull on any sense input of SQSO-ICX-001 D §3.7 (RID SMA-B02)

FRAM failure handling: every record written to both FRAMs (U3 and the mirror U36, CS# PD7) and read from the mirror when U3 fails or gives no copy that passes its CRC. Both unreadable: after three consecutive failed one-minute checks the FRAM is declared failed (HK1 `FR=1`) and the safe defaults stay (TX-OFF, commissioning hold); FRAM_BYPASS (0x0B, argument `FRM!`, accepted only then) makes the CRC-protected RAM copies of the TX-OFF latch and the operations record authoritative (`FR=2`): the check verifies their CRCs (a mismatch settles toward TX-OFF and the hold) and writes the FRAM best effort; TX-OFF by command latches at once. The mode ends when three consecutive checks read back what was written, and at every reset (RID SMA-B10)

TX_TEMP plausibility: a reading at or below −50 °C (the open line, 0 V with the 1 MΩ pull-down) or above +125 °C, rising faster than 5 °C/s (measured over at least 15 s) or more than 60 °C from the OBC board temperature is a sensor fault, logged once (HK2 `PT`); while it lasts the downlink's temperature hold uses the board temperature plus 15 °C, with the duty limit as before; ten plausible readings clear it. The PA temperature scale is × 1.011 for the 10 kΩ into the 1 MΩ pull-down (RID SMA-B19)

EPS controller supervision (SQSO-ICD-001 1.6 §4.6): the software shall write 0x5A to OBC_HEARTBEAT (0x8C) every 30 s (the controller power-cycles the OBC after 600 s without one, at most 3 times in 24 h), report EPS_SUPV (0x8F) and the refused heartbeats in HK2 (`SV`), raise the AntS supply through ANTS_PWR (0x8D, 0xA6) when neither AntS controller answers with DEPLOY_EN high and lower it at the deployment's stop, and on EPS_DISABLE_TRACKERS (0x15) write TRK_DISABLE (0x8E) with its key 0x96 and the mask (RIDs SMA-B09, SMA-B06, SMA-B17)

Wings-stowed cold hold: while SOLAR_SENSE reads the wings not deployed and the battery's minimum over the last orbit (95 one-minute minima) is below +3 °C, the software shall hold the mode at SAFE (IDLE and ACTIVE go to SAFE, no automatic return to IDLE) so the heater gets the whole surplus; the hold ends when the wings read deployed or the orbit minimum reaches +4 °C (RID THM-03; THERMAL_ANALYSIS 2.2 §6.8)

Sensor rail turn-on: a commanded ADCS sensor rail turn-on takes up to 0.55 s (R_FAULT 220 kΩ, SQSO-OBC-BRD-001 E §9.1); the software shall use a sensor only 0.6 s after its rail's enable, and again only 0.6 s after a trip on the rail has cleared, and shall not count a readback low within 0.6 s of the enable as a trip

AntS temperature gate (decision C-18, THERMAL_ANALYSIS 2.4 §4.4): before each antenna attempt the software shall power the AntS controller for 1 s and read its own temperature (command 0xC0, a documented assumption until the ISIS ICD confirms it, SQSO-MFG-003 §12 V-1); at or above −17 °C (the −20 °C qualified minimum plus 3 °C of sensor tolerance) the attempt goes ahead; colder, or with no valid answer, the attempt is deferred to the next 50-minute slot without being spent, the controller powered down; after 30 deferrals (about 25 h) the antenna is deployed whatever the reading, in sunlight after 20 min of continuous sun (the sun sensors or the array; THERMAL_ANALYSIS 2.4 §4.4: late in a sunlit period, about −13 °C), waiting at most 100 min for it; after 3 consecutive unknown readings the analysis schedule replaces the gate: the antenna is deployed after the first 20 min of continuous sun from separation + 69 min (same 100-min bound), and a valid reading returns to the gate (RID P3F-G-02); DEPLOY_RETRY (0x50) with its second byte 1 deploys the antenna at once; the deferrals, the deferral slot's elapsed time, the unknown-reading count and the force flag are persisted, so a reset neither spends a deferral nor loses the force (RID P3F-A-04); the deferrals and the last temperature are reported in HK1 `AD`. The 30-minute wait and the wings-first order are unchanged

Payload hard limits in the batch schedule (MSC L2-05): a Jetson batch starts only within the payload's hard limits (ACTIVE, sunlit, SOC at least 55 %) and ends at once when one of them fails; the hard-limit condition is still logged as a fault if the Jetson is on outside them (SIL finding SIL-39)

Transmitters silent while the AntS deployment is pending (decision C-19, SIL finding SIL-37): the software shall keep every transmitter off (beacon, housekeeping, acknowledgement, dump and GNSS frames, and the transponder), the command receiver on, while the AntS deployment is pending: from boot through the 30-minute wait and the wings, and while the AntS temperature gate defers it (SRS-F165). The downlink starts when the AntS reads deployed (every element's switch, SRS-F089) or when its sequence ends (its attempts spent, or the attempt made at the 30-deferral cap finished), whichever is first, and never before the 45-minute RF silence (SRS-F087), which is separate. The end is persisted and latched: a later DEPLOY_RETRY does not silence the stowed-antenna beacon again; only GSE ARM or a blank or corrupt deployment record (both restart the sequence) clear it. The hold is not in force while deployment is inhibited by command

Exciter keying watch (SOFTWARE_HAZARD_ANALYSIS §9.8.1, SW-HAZ-014 control C-014-9; the beacon path's TNC_PTT bypasses the transponder heartbeat and its 120 s timer): the software shall latch TX-OFF (RF_TX_EN low, persisted, as the TX_DISABLE latch) and log a critical fault, once per episode, while PTT_EXCITER reads high and: (a) it has been keyed for more than 6 s in all with the repeat path not keyed (XPDR_KEY low) and no downlink frame outstanding (the frame's estimated air window), counted across the gaps between transponder overs and cleared only by PTT_EXCITER reading low, so a stuck TNC_PTT is found in a busy transponder session; (b) XPDR_KEY reads high more than 1 s after the transponder heartbeat stopped; or (c) XPDR_KEY reads high for more than 130 s without a break (the 120 ± 4.6 s key-down timer and a margin): the repeat path explains the keying only while the heartbeat is issued and for one over (RID P3F-A-02); the watch re-arms when PTT_EXCITER reads low; recovery is the TX-OFF latch's (TX_ENABLE)

AntS reads only while powered (RID P3F-A-01): the software shall read the AntS (status and temperature, I2C3) only after raising its supply SW8 (the master arm DEPLOY_EN, no burn line; the AntS side of the I2C3 buffer is on the same supply) for at least 1 s, and lower it after the read: before each attempt (a deployed AntS is never fired), after each attempt's burn (the verification read), never while deployment is inhibited

Selector telemetry (RID SMA-15; SQSO-PAY-SEL-001 §6.4): the selector shall count, per head (H1 beacon template, H2 transponder bucket, H3 power-mode preference), its decisions and its abstentions since boot, and report them, with whether a selector table is in use, in HK2 field `SL`; verified at the selector's implementation (SQSO-PAY-SEL-001 §9; until then the table is absent and the counts are 0)

ADCS geometry preset (decision C-21): the software shall use preset 0 (both wings) unless the ground has selected another by ADCS_SET_GEOMETRY (persisted), whatever SOLAR_SENSE reads; it shall never select a one-wing or no-wing preset by itself; the preset in use and the body-frame sun vector are reported in HK2 `GE` and `SN` for the commissioning identification (COMMISSIONING_PLAN)

No empty frame (RID P3F-A-05): every downlink formatter shall produce a non-empty information field that fits its frame for any value of its inputs (each field clamped to a fixed width, the widest case shown by a test, or the text cut into frames of whole fields), and the software shall refuse and log a frame with an empty information field rather than send it; the GNSS fix is plausible only with PDOP at most 99.9

From the release of any reset (power-up of RADIO_3V3, watchdog or other), the firmware shall have the CC1200 receiving on the configured uplink frequency and USART2 accepting KISS frames within 50 ms

Until its initialisation is complete, the firmware shall hold TNC_PTT (PA8), TONE_OK (PA7) and RX_ALIVE (PB7) low, hold DAC1 and DAC2 at mid-scale (1.55 V), and configure every pin not used by §3.1 as an analog input
The firmware shall emit no RX_ALIVE pulse earlier than 100 ms after any reset

The independent watchdog (IWDG, on the LSI) shall be started in hardware mode by the option bytes at every reset, with a timeout of 250 ms nominal and at most 0.35 s with the LSI's tolerance, and shall be refreshed only from the main loop after that pass's health checks, never from an interrupt

After any reset the firmware shall start as from power-up (unkeyed, TONE_OK low, KISS parameters at their defaults, queued frames discarded), record the reset cause, and count the watchdog resets since power-up for the STATUS answer

The firmware shall run the core and buses from HSI16 at 16 MHz, SPI1 at 8 MHz for the CC1200 and the LMX2571 and at 1 MHz for the CMX138A, with no clock output (MCO off) and no other clock frequency in the flight build
The firmware shall keep SPI1 at 1 MHz (CMX138A accesses) to at most 1 ms in any 10 s
The firmware shall run USART2 (PA2 TX, PA3 RX) at 9600 baud, 8 data bits, no parity, 1 stop bit, full duplex, without flow control
The firmware shall frame and unframe KISS (FEND 0xC0, FESC 0xDB, TFEND 0xDC, TFESC 0xDD) in both directions, on port 0 only, and ignore frames for any other port

For each KISS data frame (command 0x00) of 1 to 328 bytes from the OBC, the firmware shall transmit that frame once, in order of arrival, adding the flags, FCS, bit stuffing, NRZI and AFSK; a data frame longer than 328 bytes after unescaping shall be discarded whole and counted

The firmware shall apply the KISS parameter commands TXDELAY (0x01), P (0x02), SLOTTIME (0x03), TXTAIL (0x04) and FULLDUPLEX (0x05) to the next transmission, and set them at every reset to TXDELAY 30, P 255, SLOTTIME 0, TXTAIL 1, FULLDUPLEX 1
The firmware shall apply a TXDELAY above 50 (500 ms) as 50, a TXTAIL above 5 (50 ms) as 5, and FULLDUPLEX 0 as 1

On a SetHardware frame (command 0x06) with sub-command STATUS (0x01), the firmware shall answer within 100 ms with a SetHardware frame, sub-command 0x81, carrying in order: firmware version (1 byte), the six supervision criteria (bit n set = criterion n+1 met), the noise floor and its calibrated value (dBm, signed byte each), the carrier-sense count (16 bits), the frames decoded (16 bits) and the uptime (s, 32 bits), multi-byte fields big-endian, followed by the extension of TNC-I007

The STATUS answer shall continue after the 12 bytes of TNC-I006 with, in order: the key-down limit trips, the duty backstop trips, the frames from the OBC discarded, the frames not keyed for want of TX permit or lock, the configuration scrub corrections and the watchdog resets since power-up (1 byte each, saturating), the trim and calibration record flags (1 byte: bit 0 trim record invalid, bit 1 noise-floor table invalid), and the image CRC-16 (2 bytes, big-endian); the whole answer after the command byte shall be at most 24 bytes

The firmware shall ignore every SetHardware sub-command other than 0x01, the KISS return command (0xFF) and every unknown command byte, with no effect on the radio; no command shall change a frequency, a trim, the calibration record or the flash
A USART framing, noise or overrun error inside a KISS frame shall discard that frame; the decoder shall resynchronise at the next FEND and count the error
The firmware shall hold at least 2 data frames from the OBC waiting for transmission; a frame arriving with the queue full shall be discarded and counted

For each frame accepted by TNC-F011, the firmware shall send the OBC a KISS data frame on port 0 (command 0x00) with the frame from the first address byte through the information field, without the FCS, in order of reception, starting within 100 ms of the closing flag; it shall buffer at least 2 such frames and count any discarded for a full buffer
The firmware shall send a STATUS answer only between whole KISS frames, never inside one
In the flight build USART1 shall be disabled (its pins analog) and no input other than those of §3.1 shall change the firmware's behaviour

For each transmission the firmware shall send HDLC flags (0x7E) for TXDELAY, then the frame and its FCS (CRC-16/X.25, low byte first) with a 0 stuffed after five consecutive 1s, NRZI-coded (a 0 is a change of tone), then flags for TXTAIL and at least one closing flag

The firmware shall NRZI-decode the demodulated bits, find the flags, remove the stuffed bits, check the FCS, and accept only frames of 17 to 330 bytes (FCS included) with a whole number of octets and a valid FCS; it shall discard any other frame and any frame ended by an abort (seven 1s), and count them

The firmware shall pass every frame accepted by TNC-F011 to the OBC whatever its addresses, control, PID or information field; it shall not interpret, authenticate, alter, reorder or originate frames, and shall hold no key material
Bytes received over RF shall never reach the KISS command parser: only USART2 input shall be parsed as KISS commands
The firmware shall keep receiving and passing frames while it transmits
The firmware shall read every CC1200 CFM sample on its CLKEN_CFM interrupt (GPIO0 to PB10) at 12.5 kS/s while receiving, and count missed samples
The AFSK 1200 (Bell 202) demodulator shall decode at least 90 % of 60-byte frames at an input of −114 dBm at the board's 70 cm port, ±3.0 kHz deviation, at carrier offsets of 0 and ±2.5 kHz
TNC-P001 shall hold with the 2200 Hz tone from 3 dB below to 6 dB above the 1200 Hz tone
On synthesised CFM sample files with white noise at C/N₀ 53.0 dB-Hz, the demodulator shall decode at least 90 % of 1,000 frames of 60 bytes in the host test
The firmware shall assert TNC_PTT only to transmit a data frame received from the OBC (TNC-I003), and shall generate no frame, beacon, identification, tone or carrier of its own

The firmware shall not assert TNC_PTT while TX_PERMIT_HW (PA1) reads low, and shall discard and count a frame due then; if TX_PERMIT_HW falls during a transmission it shall drop TNC_PTT within 1 ms and discard the rest of the frame

After asserting TNC_PTT the firmware shall start the frame's bits only at the end of TXDELAY and only with LMX_LD (PB14) high; if LMX_LD is low then, or falls during the frame, it shall drop TNC_PTT within 1 ms, discard the frame and count it

The firmware shall release TNC_PTT no later than 5.0 s after asserting it, whatever the frame, the parameters or the state of the modulator, by a hardware timer compare that drives PA8 low independently of the frame logic, and count each such release
The firmware shall keep TNC_PTT high for at most 60 s in any 120 s, and shall not start a transmission that would exceed it (the frame discarded and counted)

The modulator shall generate phase-continuous Bell 202 AFSK, mark 1200 Hz and space 2200 Hz, from a 12-bit sine table at 50 kS/s on DAC1 (PA4) by DMA, at 1200 bit/s, with each tone and the bit rate within ±0.5 % from −40 to +85 °C
Both tones shall have the same amplitude within 0.5 dB, without pre-emphasis, at the level set by the calibration record, so that the beacon's peak deviation is ±3.0 ± 0.15 kHz
With TNC_PTT low the firmware shall hold DAC1 at mid-scale (1.55 V)

The firmware shall count a keying-path fault when, for more than 10 ms, PTT_EXC (PB6) reads high with TNC_PTT and XPDR_KEY (PB15) low, or low with TNC_PTT and TX_PERMIT_HW high, and report the count in the STATUS extension
The firmware shall write each CFM sample to DAC2 (PA5) within one sample period (80 µs) of its CLKEN_CFM interrupt, after removing DC with a high-pass filter whose corner is at most 10 Hz
With the scale of the calibration record, an uplink at ±3.0 kHz peak deviation (1 kHz tone) shall repeat at ±3.0 ± 0.3 kHz; samples beyond the DAC range shall clip, not wrap
While the CC1200 is not receiving or its samples have stopped, the firmware shall hold DAC2 at mid-scale (1.55 V)
Through the firmware, the repeat path shall give 12 dB SINAD at an input of −120 dBm at the 70 cm port (1 kHz tone, ±3 kHz deviation), at carrier offsets of 0 and ±2.5 kHz

The firmware shall configure the CMX138A for receive, 67.0 Hz CTCSS decode, the 300–3000 Hz band filter that strips the tone, de-emphasis off, its 3.6864 MHz crystal (CLKSEL low) and IRQN on a change of tone status

The firmware shall drive TONE_OK (PA7) to follow the CMX138A's 67.0 Hz decode status (read on IRQN) within 2 ms of IRQN, high only while the CMX138A reports the tone decoded and its configuration was verified at the last scrub, and low while the CMX138A does not answer, while its configuration mismatches (until rewritten and verified) and through any reset
With the firmware's relay, the transponder shall key within 200 ms typical and 260 ms maximum of a valid 67.0 Hz tone at 6 dB SINAD and drop within 260 ms of its loss

The firmware shall configure the CC1200 for receive only in its CFM mode on the uplink frequency of the configuration record, with the 25 kHz channel filter (±7.5 kHz IF), the CFM output at 12.5 kS/s with CLKEN_CFM on GPIO0, GPIO2 as CARRIER_SENSE (IOCFG2 = 17) with the AGC_CS_THR threshold of the calibration record, GPIO1 high-impedance with CSn high (IOCFG1), and FREQOFF from the trim record
The firmware shall never issue the CC1200's STX or SFSTXON strobes and shall hold its PA power setting at the minimum

Whenever TX_PERMIT_HW is high, the LMX2571 shall hold the register image of the configuration record (the coordinated downlink frequency, FSK I2S mode, the numerator trim): the firmware shall write it within 10 ms of TX_PERMIT_HW rising, every 10 s while it stays high, and before each TNC key-up, after checking the image's CRC-32; with a bad CRC it shall write nothing, not key (TNC_PTT) and report it

Every 10 s, and at each TNC key-up, the firmware shall read back every configuration register of the CC1200 and the CMX138A, compare it with the configuration record, rewrite and re-verify any mismatch and count the correction; a mismatch that persists after 3 rewrites shall fail criterion 4 (TNC-F050)

The firmware shall take the CC1200 FREQOFF and the LMX2571 numerator trims only from the trim record in flash, each bounded to ±3 ppm; a trim outside ±3 ppm, or a record with a bad CRC, shall be replaced by a zero trim and flagged in the STATUS extension

The firmware shall toggle RX_ALIVE (PB7) every 100 ± 10 ms from the main loop, never from an interrupt, while all six criteria of TNC-F043 and TNC-F051 to TNC-F054 hold, and stop toggling while any fails (criterion 5: a hung or resetting TNC produces no pulse)
Criterion 1, CC1200 responds: every 1 s the firmware shall read PARTNUMBER (0x20 expected) and write and read back a scratch register; three consecutive failures shall fail the criterion
Criterion 2, CC1200 receiving: MARCSTATE shall read RX; when it does not, the firmware shall make one re-entry attempt, and MARCSTATE not RX for more than 2 s shall fail the criterion

Criterion 3, synthesizer and reference: the CC1200 shall report lock in RX and a stable crystal oscillator, and CLKEN_CFM interrupts shall arrive at 12.5 kHz ± 5 %; no interrupt for more than 100 ms in RX shall fail the criterion

Criterion 6, front end not deaf (TNC-FW-NF): every 60 s the firmware shall take the 10th percentile of the in-channel RSSI of that window, excluding samples with carrier sense, as the noise floor, and compare it with the calibrated floor interpolated from the record's three-temperature table at the MCU's internal temperature sensor; a floor more than 5 dB below the calibrated value in 3 consecutive windows shall fail the criterion, and a rise shall never fail it; with a table whose CRC fails, the criterion shall not be evaluated (it does not stop RX_ALIVE) and the calibrated value shall be reported as −128 dBm
The firmware shall count the rising edges of CARRIER_SENSE (GPIO2 on PB11) and report the count and the last window's noise floor in the STATUS answer
When criterion 1, 2 or 3 fails, the firmware shall re-initialise the CC1200 (reset through CC_RESETN, full configuration) at most once per 10 s, and resume RX_ALIVE when every criterion holds again

The configuration and calibration records (uplink and downlink frequencies, LMX2571 image, CC1200 and CMX138A images, frequency trims, AGC_CS_THR, the noise-floor table at three temperatures, the AFSK and repeat-audio scales) shall be written only by a ground calibration build through SWD, never by the flight build

Each record shall carry a version and a CRC-32; at start-up the firmware shall check them, use a compiled-in default for an invalid record (zero trims; criterion 6 not evaluated) and report it in the STATUS extension

The flight build shall contain no bootloader or flash-programming path reachable from USART2, USART1, RF or any GPIO, and its option bytes shall boot from main flash whatever the BOOT0 pin, with readout protection level 1 and write protection on the image
At start-up the firmware shall compute the CRC-16 of its image and report it, with its version, in the STATUS answer

The firmware shall be written in Rust (2024 edition, `no_std`) for `thumbv7em-none-eabihf` with the toolchain pinned for the OBC (`software/rust/rust-toolchain.toml`), and shall take its KISS, AX.25 and CRC code from `sqso-protocol`

The logic that implements the SC requirements shall be in a crate with `unsafe` forbidden, built and tested on the host; `unsafe` shall appear only in the board-support layer, each block with its safety argument
The firmware shall allocate no dynamic memory, use no recursion and bound every loop

Flash use shall be at most 75 % of 256 KB, RAM (static plus the worst-case stack by analysis) at most 75 % of 64 KB, and the worst-case CPU load at most 70 % at 16 MHz with the demodulator, modulator, repeat audio and scrub running together
The modules that implement the SC requirements shall have 100 % line and 100 % condition coverage in the host tests, every uncovered line marked and justified; the rest at least 90 % of lines
The firmware shall be its own configuration item with a version number, built and tested in CI on every change, and released under the release procedure

From any reset until its initialisation is complete, the firmware shall hold EOL_KEY, LOCK_SET, UNLOCK, OBC_CYCLE, ANTS_EN and TDIS_T1–T4 low, keep the four SAC DAC outputs high-impedance and EPS_ALERT_N released
Within 2 s of any reset the firmware shall fill every measurement register from a complete acquisition; until then they shall read 0x00

The watchdog (WDT_A) shall be running before any output is driven, with a timeout of at most 1.5 s worst case with its clock source, serviced only from the main loop after a completed pass, and the flight build shall never stop it

After any reset (watchdog, SW9 trip and retry, brown-out, power-up) the firmware shall start as from power-up, record the reset cause (RESET_CAUSE 0x9D, ICD-001 1.7) and increment BOOT_CNT (0x50) in FRAM

The firmware shall keep its persistent data (BOOT_CNT, the tracker mask, the SOC state, the OBC-cycle history, ENERGY, the calibration constants, the AFE acceptance record) in FRAM in two copies, each with a CRC-16, write the second only after the first reads back correctly, take defaults when both fail (mask 0, no cycles, SOC from EPSC-F041, energy 0, calibration defaults flagged in EPSC_FLAGS 0x9C, ICD-001 1.7), and protect its code and constants against writes with the FRAM memory protection
The firmware shall clock the CPU and peripherals from the internal DCO locked to REFO at an integer number of megahertz, with no clock output
The firmware shall answer at the 7-bit address 0x48 on I2C2 (eUSCI_B0, P1.2 SDA, P1.3 SCL) in standard (100 kHz) and fast (400 kHz) mode, and shall never act as a master on I2C2

The firmware shall implement the write (register, data) and read (register, repeated START, data) transactions of SMART-QSO-ICD-001 §4.1 with an auto-incrementing register pointer; unmapped addresses shall read 0x00; a read of 52 bytes from 0x00 shall return 0x00–0x33
Every read transaction shall return values from one acquisition cycle, with no multi-byte value split between two updates

Multi-byte values shall be little-endian in the units of SMART-QSO-ICD-001 §5: voltages in mV (unsigned 16 bits), currents in mA (signed 16 bits, positive charging), temperatures in 0.1 °C (signed 16 bits), SOC in % (8 bits), energy in mWh (32 bits)
Writes to read-only, retired or unmapped registers shall be acknowledged and have no effect; every accepted write shall take effect within 10 ms

The firmware shall never hold SCL low for more than 1 ms, and shall release SDA and SCL and reset its I2C target within 25 ms of a stalled transaction or a bus held low; a target reset shall change no output

The firmware shall assert EPS_ALERT_N (P4.4) while VBATT is below the low-voltage threshold of ALERT_CFG or TBATT above its high-temperature threshold, or when a new fault flag latches in STATUS or CHG_INHIBIT, and release it when the OBC has read STATUS and the condition has cleared; the thresholds at reset shall be 13.80 V and +45.0 °C
The firmware shall store ALERT_CFG (0x60, 4 bytes) when written, apply it to EPSC-I007, and return to the defaults at every reset

The register addresses, keys, bit positions and units shall come from one machine-readable definition, checked in CI against the flight software's constants (`software/rust/sqso-fsw/src/eps_telemetry.rs`, `software/rust/sqso-fsw/src/eps_supervision.rs`, `software/rust/sqso-ffi/src/eps_lockout.rs`)
The firmware shall report its version at VERSION (0xF0, 2 bytes) and the CRC-16 of its image, computed at start-up, at IMAGE_CRC (0xF2, 2 bytes, ICD-001 1.7)

The firmware shall read the BQ76952 (0x08, through the ISO1540), the four INA3221s (0x40–0x43) and the ADS7138 (0x10) on its local bus at 100 kHz; on a stuck bus it shall send nine clocks and a STOP and re-initialise; a device that fails three consecutive transactions shall set STATUS.FAULT and EPSC_FLAGS (0x9C, ICD-001 1.7) bit 5, and the registers it feeds shall read 0 until it answers again

The firmware shall fill the registers from these sources: VBATT (0x10) the AFE's stack voltage; IBATT (0x12) the AFE's pack current on RS7, positive charging; VCELL1–4 (0x70–0x77) the AFE's cell voltages; TBATT (0x14) NTC1 through the ADS7138, or NTC2 (the AFE's TS1) while NTC1_BAD reads high; TBATT2 (0x78) NTC2; VSOLAR (0x20) the highest tracker input voltage; ISOLAR (0x22) the sum of the four tracker input currents; PSOLAR (0x24) and PTRACK1–4 (0x80–0x87) the tracker input powers; VBUS (0x30) and IBUS (0x32) the 5V_PA rail; IHEATER (0x88) the heater current (RS11); all through the INA3221s and the ADS7138 as SQSO-EPS-BRD-001 §11 allocates them
The firmware shall refresh every measurement register at least every 500 ms, and IMON_JET (0x8A) and F1_SNS (EPSC-F015) every 100 ms
Voltages and currents shall be within ±2 % of reading or ±10 mV and ±10 mA, whichever is larger, from −40 to +70 °C after the acceptance calibration
TBATT and TBATT2 shall be within ±1.0 °C of the pack temperature at their NTC from −20 to +60 °C, the NTCs' own tolerance included

IMON_JET (0x8A) shall report the Jetson eFuse U19's IMON (0.84 V/A at P5.0) in mA, averaged over at least 4 samples, within ±3 % of reading ±20 mA of the IMON voltage's value after the acceptance two-point calibration (the eFuse's own IMON tolerance excluded)

The firmware shall measure the four burn currents (P1.0, P1.4, P1.6, P1.7), V_BURN (P5.2) and VTRK (P5.3) every 100 ms and report them at 0x90–0x9B (ICD-001 1.7 BURN_I1–4, V_BURN, VTRK: four currents in mA, then V_BURN and VTRK in mV); a burn current above 0.4 A for more than 13 s shall set STATUS.FAULT and EPSC_FLAGS (0x9C, ICD-001 1.7) bit 3. The firmware has no output that starts or stops a burn

The firmware shall classify F1_SNS (P5.1, 1 MΩ / 220 kΩ from F1's heater pin) as intact or open with a band for each, and report a reading between the bands as neither (EOL_STATE bits 1 and 2 both 0) and flag it in EPSC_FLAGS (0x9C, ICD-001 1.7)

STATUS (0x00) shall set CHARGING (bit 7) while IBATT exceeds +5 mA, SUNLIT (bit 6) while PSOLAR exceeds 0.3 W, LOW_BATT (bit 5) while SOC is below 25 %, OVER_TEMP (bit 4) while TBATT is above +45.0 °C, UNDER_TEMP (bit 3) while TBATT is below 0.0 °C, FAULT (bit 2) per EPSC-F010, F014 and F024 or an AFE fault or permanent fail; bits 1–0 are reserved and shall read 0
The retired registers 0x01 (formerly MODE) and 0x02 (formerly LOAD_EN) shall read 0x00 and acknowledge and ignore every write: the firmware sets no mode and drives no load enable

CHG_INHIBIT (0x7A) shall report: bit 0 cold and bit 1 hot, when WIN_OK reads low with TBATT below +1.1 °C or above +44.0 °C; bit 2 a cell over-voltage from the AFE; bit 3 an AFE fault or permanent fail, or its settings disagreeing with the acceptance record (EPSC-F063); bit 4 the secondary protector's fuse blown (cell voltages present at the AFE with BAT_F absent); bit 5 the recharge lockout latched (PERMIT low while the charge window reads open, WIN_OK or NTC1_BAD high); bit 6 NTC1_BAD high
LOAD_SHED (0x7B) shall report SHED (bit 0) and the fault lines of SW1 (bit 1) and SW3 (bit 2); the firmware shall take no part in the shed
The firmware shall sample every switch fault line (FLT_SW1–SW8, FLT_SW11, FLT_EFUSE) at least every 10 ms, count each assertion longer than 10 ms, and latch STATUS.FAULT until the OBC has read STATUS

The firmware shall compute SOC (0x16) from the BQ76952's coulomb counter on RS7 (IBATT, the AFE's pack current) against a learnt capacity: at each end of charge (pack at or above 16.30 V with the charge current below 20 mA) it shall reset the count to the charge that the end-of-charge voltage gives on the cell's OCV curve and update the capacity estimate with a weight of 0.1; SOC shall be clamped to 0–100 %

When the FRAM's SOC state is invalid, the firmware shall start SOC from the lowest cell voltage through the OCV table and set EPSC_FLAGS (0x9C, ICD-001 1.7) bit 0 (SOC uncalibrated) until the first end of charge
After the first end of charge, SOC shall be within ±5 % (absolute) of the pack's true state of charge throughout the mission, ageing included
While the lowest cell voltage is below 3.30 V, the SOC reported shall not exceed the OCV-table value for that voltage plus 5 %
ENERGY (0x40) shall accumulate the energy delivered to the bus loads (VBAT × the bus-load current) in mWh and be saved to FRAM at least every 10 min

For each enabled tracker the firmware shall run perturb-and-observe on its SAC DAC, from the tracker's input power (INA3221), with a step and period that give a tracking efficiency of at least 98 % at constant irradiance and at least 95 % with irradiance ramps of 10 % per second
The firmware shall command no string set point outside 3.3–5.4 V
While the CV or CC loop governs (pack at or above 16.30 V, or charge current at or above 0.38 A) the firmware shall hold each set point and resume tracking when the loop releases
A tracker whose input power is below 50 mW, whose INA3221 does not answer, or which is disabled by TRK_DISABLE shall have its DAC output high-impedance

The firmware shall raise LOCK_SET (P4.0) for 1.0 ± 0.1 s when the AFE reports its Safety Cell Undervoltage permanent fail, or when every AFE reading over 5 s shows a cell below 2.00 V with each reading plausible (a valid transaction, four cells read, their sum within 5 % of the stack voltage); once per event, a new event needing every cell at or above 2.50 V and no permanent fail in between; each event recorded in FRAM and in EPSC_FLAGS (0x9C, ICD-001 1.7) bit 6
The firmware shall raise LOCK_SET for no other reason

On a write of 0xC5 to LOCK_UNLOCK (0x7D) the firmware shall raise UNLOCK (P4.1) for 1.0 ± 0.1 s and then lower it; any other value shall lower it at once; it shall be low at every reset; each raise needs its own write

The firmware shall send the BQ76952 only read commands and the subcommands that read its data memory and status: it shall not enter CONFIG_UPDATE, write data memory or OTP, change its security state, reset a permanent fail or command its FETs, and the image shall contain no unseal or full-access key. Every 10 min it shall read the AFE's protection settings (COV, CUV, OCD1, SCD, OCC, UTC, OTC, OTD, SUV) and compare them with the acceptance record in FRAM, reporting a difference in CHG_INHIBIT bit 3 and EPSC_FLAGS (0x9C, ICD-001 1.7) bit 4 without any corrective write

The firmware shall raise EOL_KEY (P4.2) and set EOL_STATE bit 3 only on a write of 0x3C to EOL_KEY (0x7E) followed within 1.0 s by a write of 0xC3, and only if, at the second write, EOL_ARMED reads low and F1_SNS reads intact

The firmware shall lower EOL_KEY and clear bit 3 at the first of: 10.0 s after the raise; a write to 0x7E other than the expected next byte; EOL_ARMED reading high; any reset. EOL_KEY shall never be high for more than 10.0 s while the firmware runs, nor for more than 11.5 s with a hang (EPSC-F003)

A refused sequence (wrong value or order, more than 1.0 s between the writes, or a precondition false) shall leave EOL_KEY low and bit 3 clear, and be counted in EOL_REFUSED (0x9E, ICD-001 1.7, saturating at 255)
EOL_STATE (0x7C) shall report EOL_ARMED (bit 0), F1 open (bit 1) and F1 intact (bit 2) from EPSC-F015, and EOL_KEY high (bit 3), from samples at most 100 ms old
A write of 0x5A to OBC_HEARTBEAT (0x8C) shall count as a heartbeat; any other value shall be ignored
After 600–660 s without a heartbeat, and not earlier than 600 s after the controller's start or its last cycle, the firmware shall raise OBC_CYCLE (P6.1) for 2.5 ± 0.3 s and then lower it

The firmware shall make at most 3 cycles in any 24 h, then stop the supervision and set EPS_SUPV bit 7; 10 consecutive heartbeats shall clear the count and bit 7; the history shall be kept in FRAM so that a controller reset neither restarts the supervision early nor loses the count
No command shall disable the supervision
EPS_SUPV (0x8F) shall report the disabled trackers (bits 0–3), ANTS_EN from the controller (bit 4), the cycles in the last 24 h (bits 5–6) and the supervision stopped (bit 7)
A write of 0xA6 to ANTS_PWR (0x8D) shall raise ANTS_EN (P6.0) for at most 1,800 s (−0/+60 s), then lower it; any other value shall lower it at once; it shall be low at every reset

A two-byte write to TRK_DISABLE (0x8E) of the key 0x96 and a mask (bits 0–3 disable T1–T4) shall set TDIS_T1–T4 (P6.2–P6.5) within 10 ms and store the mask in FRAM; a write without the key shall be ignored; at start-up the stored mask shall be applied, or none if both copies fail
A TRK_DISABLE write whose mask disables all four trackers, or sets a bit above bit 3, shall be refused with a NACK and no change

The firmware shall be written in C11 (ISO/IEC 9899:2011) to MISRA C:2012, with a recorded deviation list, and the JPL D-60411 rules of `docs/development/CODING_STANDARDS.md`, compiled with TI's MSP430-GCC (`msp430-elf-gcc`) at a version pinned when coding starts and recorded in the software version description, without an RTOS

The hardware-independent logic (register map and keyed registers, timers, SOC, MPPT decisions, lockout, EOL key and supervision) shall be in modules built both for the target and for the host, and tested on the host with the project's CMocka suites in CI
The firmware shall allocate no dynamic memory, use no recursion and bound every loop

Code and constants shall use at most 75 % of the 32 KB FRAM, RAM (static plus the worst-case stack by analysis) at most 75 % of the 4 KB SRAM, and the main loop's worst-case period shall be at most 100 ms

The modules that implement the SC requirements shall reach 100 % MC/DC on the host with GCC's condition coverage (`-fcondition-coverage`, GCC 14 or later), every uncovered condition justified; the other modules at least 90 % of lines
The firmware shall build without warnings at `-Wall -Wextra -Werror`, and a MISRA C:2012 checker shall run on every change

The flight build shall have no path that changes its own image (no call into the bootstrap loader, no FRAM program write outside EPSC-F005's data areas); the controller shall be programmed only on the ground through J22
The firmware shall be its own configuration item with a version number, built and tested in CI on every change, and released under the release procedure
